# 2026-10-28: scripts/cliff-bench on #13726 (merged with main at 5acfabebb). The last pin predates #13677, which grew checker.fern with the unsafe obligation pass and the handle rules.
# 2026-10-26: PR13578 CI40354664618 at b2c7c6251 measured 38,503,920 bytes / 365,557 crossings. Main a4f676d26 already measured 38,494,112 / 365,552.
# 2026-10-25: Perf run 40200803636 (main at 127eb63c). checker.fern grew with today's merges: +5.0% cliff count, +5.3% bytes.
# 2026-10-23: combined source 160186731f, Perf run 40026009089. The receiver checks and FIP table add compiler source.
# rc==1 append-cliff baselines for the SELF-HOST COMPILER, checked against
# every run by scripts/ci-check-perf (the same comparator the instruction-count
# gate uses — one tool, two baselines).
#
# FORMAT: metric  value  [tolerance%]. The key is <arch>/checker.cliff_<bytes|count>,
# produced by scripts/cliff-bench compiling compiler/checker.fern with
# the self-hosted compiler under FERN_CLIFF_REPORT=1.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. docs/LOCAL-DEV-LOOP.md recorded this exact workload at
# 188 crossings / 812 bytes on 2026-08-04 and called it noise. By 2026-08-16 it
# was 77,985 crossings and 21.4 GB — a seven-order-of-magnitude regression that
# went twelve days unnoticed because nothing measured it outside a human typing
# an env var (#6911).
#
# IT IS NOT A CEILING, AND A MOVE UPWARD IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY A REGRESSION.
# The subject is the self-host compiler compiling checker.fern, so the number
# scales with the compiler's OWN sources: every feature that adds `ir.Op`s
# through the lowering, or names through checker.Scope.bind, adds
# appends and therefore bytes. Between f350a01 and ce72d61 it rose 12% with no
# regression in it — 8d3fef0 (`if let` / `let … else` on the shared pattern
# grammar, #2698) accounts for 5.8% of that on its own, and d61e5d3 (a
# self-host rc fix that stopped a struct rebind freeing a shared box's field)
# bought 18% more crossings as the price of being correct. Read a move here as
# a QUESTION — which commit, and did it add compiler or add copying — and
# update the number in the same PR when the answer is the former.
#
# THE FIRST BASELINE WAS NEVER MEASURED AT THE COMMIT THAT CARRIED IT. f350a01
# checked in 268,028,888 / 282,154; re-measured, that commit reads 377,583,648
# / 358,568 (#7545). The 268 M figure and the gdb census agreeing with it to 3%
# both describe some earlier commit, so treat the paragraphs below as history
# rather than as readings of anything still in the tree.
#
# THE NUMBERS JUMPED WHEN THE INSTRUMENT DID, once. Every reading before
# #6888 §4d.6 counted SCALAR-element appends only: the tally lived inside
# `__fern_arr_push_grow`, and `T[]` / `string[]` appends go through
# `__fern_arr_push_grow_ptr` / `_str` (and their `_move_` siblings), which
# bumped nothing. So "988 bytes" was never this workload's copying — it was
# its `i32[]` copying. Every variant tallies now, and the same commit,
# unchanged, reads 281,621 crossings / 267,661,872 bytes. An independent gdb
# breakpoint census of the same compile agrees to within 3% (273,382 copies
# over 33,385,176 pointer elements), which is what says the new reading is the
# instrument working rather than a regression.
#
# So the historical narrative below reads one element type only: 21.4 GB fell
# to 3.07 GB when the x86 assembler's state parameter became `own`, and 3.07 GB
# fell to 988 bytes when `fieldPlaceAppendCopies` stopped treating a container
# handed to a SCALAR-returning call as captured (#6911). Both were real wins on
# what was measured. Neither made the self-host compiler stop copying its
# `ir.Op[]`: 267 MB of the 267 MB below is `irlower.LowerState.emit` and
# `checker.Scope.bind`, the ratchet docs/PERFORMANCE-AUDIT-2026-08.md §4d.5 is
# about, and it was there the whole time.
#
# BYTES ARE THE RANKING KEY. The count is recorded too, but never scope work
# against it alone — docs/LOCAL-DEV-LOOP.md has two rounds of `own`-conversion
# aimed at sites that could not have paid, because 188 crossings of a 4-byte
# loop-depth stack outnumber one accumulator copying gigabytes. A count that
# halves while the bytes hold flat is not an improvement, and this gate will
# say so by only flagging the bytes line.
#
# APPENDS ONLY. Both metrics come from `__fern_arr_push`'s un-share path, so a
# quadratic `.with` (copy-on-write through `__fern_arr_cow_inplace`) is INVISIBLE
# here — it moves neither number. #6911 makes the point: lifting the buffer out
# of the struct for the `.with` patch loops moved nothing on this gate and took
# the compile from 97 s to 19 s. A flat line here is not a statement about
# copying in general.
#
# NOR IS THE BYTE COUNT A COST. The last 3.07 GB was on a `string[]`, so every
# crossing also inc'd each element and the discarded copy dec'd each one back:
# 3 GB of memcpy, but ~30% of the compile in rc traffic around it. Weigh the
# ELEMENT TYPE, not just the weight.
#
# EXACT, so the 1% default tolerance is a significance threshold rather than a
# noise floor: two runs on one commit reproduce these to the digit (verified
# when the gate landed). ADVISORY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, like the other gates —
# when the number moves on purpose, update it in the same PR.
#
# Only x86_64 is measured today: cliff-bench runs on whichever host it is given,
# and the aarch64 lane does not yet build a self-host compiler for it. An
# unbaselined arch reports UNBASELINED rather than failing.
#
# Re-pinned 2026-09-03 (#8172) after the assembler's CFI recorder stopped
# appending its rule arrays through a borrowed spread: 5,177,184,636 / 568,878
# on the same tree the line before, 94.6% of it that one site. What is left is
# the compiler's own accumulators (§4d.5) plus the recorder's linear residue.

# Re-pinned 2026-09-03 (#8190) after fieldPlaceAppendCopies started consulting
# the callee escape summary: a container read into a call argument the callee
# provably cannot leak no longer counts as a binding that names it, so the
# field append keeps its in-place grow. 271,315,168 / 379,810 on the same tree
# the line before. The arm64 TARGET, which this was aimed at and which no
# baseline covers, went 1,290,816,360 / 510,568 to 376,513,680 / 474,940.

# Re-pinned 2026-09-04 (#7397) after the #4873 containment bracket gained three
# field- and path-granular deaths: it no longer retains a struct argument's
# array field across a call the field cannot be read back through, no longer
# treats a read whose enclosing block RETURNS before mentioning the name again
# as non-final (except at an ARRAY parameter position, where the withdrawn
# bracket hands the superseded buffer to a dec that does not free — the
# conformance leak census reads that as 115 extra live blocks), and admits a
# local unpacked from a call result's field. The parent, a5cea3cd2, measures
# 203,065,352 / 376,907; `irlower.LowerState.emit` went 156,918,008 / 35,105 to
# 132,890,016 / 28,991 of that, and `checker.Scope.bind` 22,383,696 / 244,028 to
# 21,381,760 / 277,542 (a gdb census at 9e2993249, 0.07% off these totals).
#
# THE COUNT ROSE 7% WHILE THE BYTES FELL 12%, and that is the expected shape,
# not a regression to chase: an append that grows in place hands its buffer
# back at rc 2 (the identity convention), so the NEXT append on it crosses —
# where a forced copy would have handed back a fresh rc-1 buffer instead. The
# trade is one whole-buffer copy for a later small one, which is why
# `Scope.bind`'s mean copy fell from 92 to 77 bytes while it crossed more often.

# Re-pinned 2026-10-11 (#12117): 75,047,896 / 238,346 to 30,008,120 / 198,714.
# seminline.resolve decides a read's resolution before it writes the edits, so
# its appends no longer copy the edits held for the rollback (32.4 MB of it);
# the rest is semsource's state threaded past attempts, a part phi per read of
# a split construction, and a carried reuse donor held past an arm's body.
# docs/rc-log/2026-10-11-c-the-state-is-not-held-past-an-attempt.md attributes
# what is left: semsource.define 4.7 MB, seminline.part_of 2.6 MB.
#
# Re-pinned 2026-10-15 (#12418): 33,052,304 / 236,323 on main (the previous
# pin was drift) to 33,306,720 / 239,924, semreach's facts grown per function.
#
# Re-pinned 2026-10-28 (#13768): 39,645,312 / 371,072 to 40,432,712 / 388,867.
# Main measured these values at eb0e5fdc0, and the run on #13768 agrees.
